verdicts.conditionQuote: If the server has already completed a request with that key
verdicts.claimQuote: it returns the stored result instead of performing the operation again
verdicts.note: This is the core mechanism claim itself (its 'if' is the trigger of the behaviour), not a limit on some other claim.

verdicts.conditionQuote: Keys only protect against duplicates while the server still remembers them. In this design, stored results expire after 24 hours, so a retry sent after that window is treated as a new payment.
verdicts.claimQuote: If the server has already completed a request with that key, it returns the stored result instead of performing the operation again.
verdicts.note: After 24 hours a retry with the same key is performed again, so u2's claim is false in that case.

verdicts.conditionQuote: if a client reuses a key with a different amount, the server must reject the request rather than return the old result
verdicts.claimQuote: it returns the stored result instead of performing the operation again
verdicts.note: A same-key request with different parameters is rejected, not answered with the stored result, so u2 read alone is misleading.

verdicts.conditionQuote: within a bounded window; they are not a general guarantee against duplicate operations
verdicts.note: Intra-sentence summary condition restating c2/c3; dropping 'within a bounded window' makes the summary claim false.
